9.9Actor State Snapshots ​

An auditable snapshot must contain at least the following.

SectionWhat to RecordOutput Ceiling
Observation boundariesActor, time window, observation position, and data cutoffLimit to the current sample
Circles and rolesMemberships, roles, conflicts, and ability to enter and exitDo not assume identification with the circle or common goals
Slow, intermediate-timescale, and fast variablesStatus, source, time, and counterevidence for each variableDo not judge the essence of personality
Conditions in both channelsMaterial conditions and experience–meaning conditionsDo not substitute either for the other
Competing explanationsStructural factors, roles, strategies, measurement, and chanceRetain explanations that cannot be distinguished
Privacy and usesPrivacy level, authorization, and prohibited usesStay within the limits on use
Update conditionsWhich variables a new event reaches and when to review themDo not update every state at once

The snapshot retains its observation cutoff and the time at which information was obtained. When a new event occurs, first determine which channels and time bands it reaches and then update the corresponding variables. Calculate autonomous changes triggered by the passage of time itself separately under the registered rules for dynamics. When neither a new observation nor a reliable rule for advancing the state is available, the last observed value and its time can be retained or the state can be marked unknown. The old value must not be treated as the actual current state. Rerunning the model is likewise no evidence that all variables changed at once.

9.9Note

Understanding this section

9.9 Agent-state snapshots

A state snapshot is a bounded record with sources, a cutoff, and a purpose. It can show what was known then and on what grounds, but is not a complete real-time replica of a person; refreshing the file also does not refresh the real-world state.

Line 2055 of the Chinese source calls it an ‘auditable snapshot’ (translated from Chinese), emphasizing that others can trace how records support conclusions, not that a complete form certifies correct personality judgments. A snapshot should preserve distinctions among materials, observations, and inferences; an old variable value, a current projected value, and a genuinely new observation must not share indistinguishable markings. [T-99；T-evidence]

The first row, ‘observation boundaries’, requires the agent, time window, observation position, and information cutoff. Observation positions may include self-report, peer observation, or administrative records, each seeing different portions. The cutoff states the latest acquisition time of information used in this output; its output ceiling is a bounded sample, not a person's entire life represented by one meeting or interface. [T-99；T-91]

The second row, ‘circles and roles’, preserves memberships, role conflicts, and capacities to enter and exit. Recording someone as still a member does not imply identification with shared goals; knowing they have been assigned responsibility does not imply resources or willingness to bear it. Role validity periods, barriers to exit, and conflicting demands affect projection and cannot be flattened into one job title. [T-99；T-roles]

The third row, ‘slow/intermediate-timescale/fast variables’, requires each item's state, source, time, and counterevidence. Evidence status and variable value are different: a candidate variable may have a conditional prediction without a checked present value; a credible old observation may no longer suffice to represent the present. A slow variable need not remain unchanged forever, and a fast variable need not change every time the model runs. [T-99；T-times；T-status]

The fourth row, ‘dual-channel conditions’, records material conditions and experience–meaning separately. Existing amounts of funding, time, or tools cannot replace personal experience, and an experience report cannot replace resource availability. If a channel is irrelevant to the task, its relevance boundary may be explained; form completeness cannot justify forced disclosure, nor may claims of autonomy or improved life be filled with totals alone. [T-99；T-channels]

The fifth row, ‘competing explanations’, retains structural, role, strategic, measurement, and chance factors. A snapshot is not a conclusion card storing only the favored story; if changed duties and short-term stress remain indistinguishable explanations of the same refusal, retain that indistinguishability. Whether the next event distinguishes them depends on new materials, not on how completely the old narrative is written. [T-99；T-status]

The sixth row, ‘privacy and use’, registers levels, authorization, and prohibited uses. The output ceiling prohibits crossing use boundaries; old materials permitted for communication do not become usable for public characterization or high-impact action merely by entering a new snapshot. When versions continue, protections and permitted uses must also continue to be checked, rather than copying content while losing its conditions. [T-99；T-privacy]

The seventh row, ‘update conditions’, states which events reach which variables and when review occurs. First find the channel an event enters, then judge whether it updates a fact, degree of support, fast variable, or role condition; variables not reached are not all rewritten with it. A formal notice may change role tasks without measuring the person's emotions, still less immediately establishing personality change. [T-99；T-times]

Line 2067 of the Chinese source requires preserving both the observation cutoff and the time information was obtained. For example, a record formed at 10:00 but arriving at the analyst at 11:00 cannot be used in a prediction frozen at 10:30. After 11:00, understanding of the past event may be revised, but it must be marked as later-acquired information; a revised historical snapshot cannot masquerade as what was known then. This connects to §9.6's boundary on hindsight variables. [T-99；T-status]

New events are not the only source of change. If time itself enters a reliable registered dynamic rule, autonomous change may be computed under that rule even without a new event; the rule, initial values, valid region, and uncertainty must be shown. Computed values are rule-based projections, not new observations. If the rule is unreliable, conditions change, or support is absent, ‘it might change with time’ cannot justify inventing a curve. [T-99]

Without new observations or a reliable advancement rule, the source permits retaining ‘the last observed value and its time’ or marking the requested present value as unknown. The former preserves history; the latter expresses a current knowledge gap. They are compatible and may appear on the same screen. Updating the file-modification time beside an old value to today cannot support a claim to have measured today's actual state. [T-99]

Fleeson's 2001 experience-sampling study supplies a concrete temporal distinction: participants were scheduled to describe behavior and feelings during a specified preceding hour; late submissions still had to describe the originally scheduled period, while devices recorded completion dates and times for excluding excessively early or late reports. The added point here separates the ‘period described’ from the ‘submission time’; obtaining a record later does not automatically make it a measurement of a later state. [P-F2001]

A useful snapshot therefore preserves three things together: the observations used at the time, the rules under which projection is now performed, and the present states still unknown. Each update changes only fields reached by materials or rules and preserves the previous version and reasons for change. Auditability may help locate errors, but without actual comparisons and reader materials this design cannot be called proven to improve prediction or understanding. [T-99；T-status]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Define the agent, observation window, observation position, and current information cutoff, establishing the scope represented by the record.

  2. 2

    Across the seven sections, supply sources, evidence statuses, counterevidence, competing explanations, privacy, and uses item by item, without inventing states to fill blanks.

  3. 3

    First preserve the event or observation time, then the acquisition time; frozen predictions use only materials available before the cutoff.

  4. 4

    When a new event arrives, locate the variables it reaches through specific channels; update different timescale bands and evidence statuses separately.

  5. 5

    If reliable autonomous dynamics have been registered, advance time with assumptions retained and separate projected values from new observations.

  6. 6

    Without new observation or a reliable rule, retain the dated last value and current unknown; rerunning cannot masquerade as refreshing every state.

  7. 7

    Preserve versions, local output ceilings, and unresolved items so review can detect hindsight information, stale values, or expanded uses.

Distinctions to keep clear

Event/observation time

The real-world time described by the material.

≠

Information-acquisition time

When the analyst obtained the material.

Last observed value

A historical record with a specified time.

≠

Current true value

Needs current observation or proportionate evidence; changing an old value’s date cannot supply it.

Rule-projected value

A calculation under explicit dynamics and premises.

≠

New observation

From a new actual measurement or record.

Updated evidentiary support

New material changes a judgment’s standing.

≠

The object changes

Requires grounds concerning object states or dynamics.

Rerun the model

Recalculate inputs under rules.

≠

Refresh every state

Not established by the run itself.

Teaching construction: a bounded snapshot and late-arriving materialTeaching scenario

AssumptionsPerson, project, materials, and permissions are explicit teaching assumptions, not actual records; a/b were obtained before cutoff and c only at 11:00.

Suppose fictional actor A participates in project P. Material a is a 09:00 role notice assigning coordination of this meeting; b is A’s 09:30 self-report, ‘I want to finish the first draft today’; c is a veto record from the 10:00 meeting, delivered to the analyst only at 11:00. A snapshot frozen at 10:30 may have seven sections: ① observation boundary: A, 09:00–10:30, with a/b obtained; ② circle/role: P’s meeting-coordination task, identification and exit conditions unknown; ③ medium variable: only b’s stated goal, with slow variables and current emotion unknown; ④ known meeting schedule, experience limited to b’s report; ⑤ role demands, strategy, and other factors remain undistinguished; ⑥ material permitted only for this meeting’s communication, prohibiting onward disclosure and personnel evaluation; ⑦ role changes or new expressions from A trigger corresponding review. The unavailable c cannot be used yet. After c arrives at 11:00, add a 10:00 behavior record without backdating it as known for the 10:30 prediction or updating personality from the veto too.

BoundaryShows fields and knowledge timing without treating a stated goal as all actual willingness; supplies no real-person snapshot or basis for punishment.

Mathematical teaching construction: explicit dynamics can operate without events, but calculation is not observationTeaching scenario

AssumptionsInitial values, rate bounds, and no-input conditions are all stipulated; this is no measurement model for fatigue, emotion, or health and estimates no actual person’s dynamics.

Let artificial state x have last known initial value x(10)=8 in abstract units, with no inputs or shocks over two hours and a nonnegative state. In model A, the decrease is fixed at 2 per hour, so x(12)=8−2×2=4. In model B, the decrease rate always lies between 1 and 3 per hour, so cumulative decrease is between 2 and 6 and x(12)∈[2,6]. Both yield results by time advancement, but if reality supports neither rate rule, retain only ‘8 at 10:00, unknown at 12:00’ rather than arbitrarily selecting 4.

Boundary4 and [2,6] are projections under their respective premises, neither a new observation at 12:00; changing unknown conditions precludes continued extrapolation.

Experience sampling in 2001: separate described intervals from completion timesDocumented case

Fleeson’s Study 1 asked 46 students to report behavior and feelings for a specified preceding hour five times daily for 13 days. Late respondents were still to describe the originally scheduled interval; handheld devices recorded completion date and time, and researchers excluded records under timing and other quality conditions.

SourceFleeson，Toward a Structure- and Process-Integrated View of Personality: Traits as Density Distributions of StatesJPSP 80(6):1011–1027, 2001; Study 1 Method, printed p. 1014/PDF 4, especially Procedure passages on scheduled reports, late completion, and time recording; Materials, printed p. 1015/PDF 5.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis section reuses the study, adding the distinction between content interval and submission time without repeating distribution-stability conclusions. Historical device timestamping does not authorize covert collection for this task; data were not recalculated, and self-report is not treated as continuous all-day or real-time truth.

What is a snapshot’s observation position?

Who observes and by what method, such as self-report, a peer’s observation, or administrative records; this bounds what can be known.

Basis: Chinese source line 2059.

If a 10:00 behavior record arrives at 11:00, may it enter the original grounds for a 10:30 prediction?

No. Revise knowledge of the past after 11:00 while preserving late arrival.

Without a new event, must a variable remain unchanged?

No. Registered, supported autonomous dynamics permit time-based calculation; without a rule, neither constancy nor decay may be assumed.

No. Check the channels reached by the event and evidence for each variable separately.

No contradiction. 8 is a historical observation with its original time; unknown is the judgment about the current state.

No. Material correspondence and traceability are not comparative validation or net-effect testing.

9.10Example of Actor Analysis in an Event ​

Suppose a project lead suddenly vetoes the team’s proposal in a public meeting. The observation record can establish only the veto, the context of the meeting, what was said, and the visible consequences. Candidate fast variables might include time pressure, physical fatigue, perceived threat, and immediate anger. Candidate intermediate-timescale variables might include project goals, responsibilities of the role, a recent decline in trust, and reputational risk. A candidate slow variable might be long-term tolerance of uncertainty, which would require evidence across contexts.

The circles must also be examined. Has management just changed the metrics? Is the team short on resources? Has public opinion on a platform raised the cost of failing publicly? Do care responsibilities at home reduce the time available? Does organizational culture reward forceful decisions? The lead’s veto may change trust and subsequent expression in the team. The team’s silence may reinforce the lead’s belief that “only coercion works,” creating feedback. Writing only “controlling personality” would obscure multiple channels open to intervention. Writing only “determined by structure” would erase the actor’s choices, responsibilities, and capability to bridge circles.

A reasonable output should separate confirmed facts about behavior from the support available for hypotheses about states. It should also specify circle conditions and channels in both directions, the next observation that would best distinguish the alternatives, and what remains unknown when evidence is insufficient. The output can enter path projection in Part 11. It cannot itself produce a diagnosis of the person, punishment, or authority to compel.

9.10Note

Understanding this section

9.10 Example of Actor Analysis within an Event

This section is a teaching scenario explicitly beginning ‘suppose’. Its task is not to characterize the person in charge, but to separate one public veto into behavior records, state candidates, circle conditions, possible feedback, and discriminating material still needed.

Chinese source line 2071 stipulates a person in charge suddenly vetoing a proposal in a public meeting, with no actual person or meeting archive. ‘Confirmed’ below therefore means only the stipulated behavior; actual analysis requires original records, contemporaneous context, expressions, and visible consequences. The guide writer cannot fill absent exact words, motives, or outcomes in as facts. [T-910; T-evidence]

Fast-variable candidates in that paragraph include time pressure, physical fatigue, perceived threat, and immediate anger. They are not four established facts and each needs material: deadlines may be checked in project documents; fatigue and perceived threat require proportionate observation or expression rather than inference from ‘sudden’. Time pressure may also have institutional conditions and need not be reduced to purely inner emotion. [T-910; T-channels]

Medium-variable candidates include project goals, role responsibility, recent declining trust, and reputational risk, focusing on constraints and expectations across rounds or phases. Whether the person bears different failure responsibilities, goals just changed, or trust declined needs independent material. A job title is not responsibility content, and one veto does not measure declining trust. [T-910; T-roles]

Slow-variable candidates include persistent tendencies such as long-term tolerance of uncertainty. They may compress differences across settings, but one meeting cannot identify a long-term pattern or justify an essential ‘controlling personality’ label from one refusal. Persistence needs time coverage, and cross-context claims need corresponding coverage; structure and roles remain competing explanations. [T-910; T-times; T-personality]

Chinese source line 2073 requires simultaneously checking five circle entry points: changed management metrics, scarce team resources, platform discourse raising public-failure costs, family care reducing available time, and organizational culture rewarding forceful decisions. Their existence and effects each await checks. Family care is a potentially relevant condition, not authority to investigate private life. If public task material already distinguishes key explanations, prefer less intrusive material. [T-910; T-privacy]

The individual veto may change team trust or later expression, while team silence may be interpreted by the person in charge as evidence that coercion works, changing later behavior. This is a candidate feedback chain requiring separate observation of members’ actual reactions, signal return, the person’s uptake, and which subsequent state or constraint changes. Quiet after a meeting does not directly establish fear, lost trust, or reinforced beliefs; independent deadline changes may affect both sides together. [T-910; T-feedback; T-95]

Personality labels alone miss changeable tasks and interfaces; ‘structure determines everything’ misses actor choices, responsibility, and cross-circle connections. The original calls for competing and connected analysis, not a fixed half-and-half allocation of explanation. Even if the environment creates pressure, check how the person acts; even if the person performed the act, blame or punishment judgments are not thereby complete. [T-910; T-roles; T-channels]

Chinese source line 2075 prescribes five output layers: evidence-supported behavior facts; support for each state hypothesis; circle conditions and two-way channels; the most discriminating next observation; and unknowns retained for insufficient evidence. A complete short output based on the setup follows, avoiding a mere list of candidates without support strengths and stopping points. [T-910]

The most discriminating observation is not ‘learn every private detail’, but appropriately obtainable material on which competing explanations give different answers. If both hypotheses explain a veto under scarce resources, seek existing records with the same task targets, visible information, and other relevant conditions while resources shift from scarce to sufficient. Whether such comparable material exists remains to be checked; discrimination does not justify forcing real people into unauthorized experiments. The threshold construction below only makes logical conditions explicit. [T-910; T-identify]

On entering Part Eleven, freeze snapshots, event identities, mechanism hypotheses, parameters or explicit unknowns, clocks, and stopping conditions. Actual observation, others’ reports, plans, hypotheses, and simulations must remain separate. The book’s manager example remains hypothetical; a path diagram does not make it actual history. Without probability material, multiple paths can remain without forcing a ‘most likely’ ranking. [T-events]

In Ross et al.’s 1977 Experiment 2, observers watched research assistants reenact earlier question-and-answer scenes and still rated questioners higher in general knowledge. This reminds us that observation alone does not guarantee a representative behavioral sample. The experiment reenacted selected scenes, not natural meetings, and cannot establish that this section’s fictional person in charge is merely a victim of circumstances or that individual differences never exist. [P-ROSS2]

Bounded analysis thus states both what to check next and what remains unsayable. Behavior records and conditional recommendations may hold, but diagnosis, punishment, and coercive authority do not arise automatically from one analysis; they require corresponding professional, normative, and authorization procedures. [T-910; T-J]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First mark the original example as a teaching hypothesis, separating stipulated facts from absent actual records without inventing dialogue or motives.

  2. 2

    Propose fast/medium/slow candidates, listing corresponding material, counterevidence, and scope for each; candidates cannot replace one another.

  3. 3

    Check circle conditions in parallel, including metrics, resources, public costs, care time, and organizational rewards, following minimally necessary acquisition.

  4. 4

    Check veto-to-team and team-to-manager chains separately; discuss feedback further only with compatible connections and subsequent change.

  5. 5

    Compare competing explanations under the same target and information, prioritizing appropriately obtainable material that changes answers.

  6. 6

    Produce five layers: behavior facts, support levels, circle channels, next observations, and retained unknowns.

  7. 7

    If projection continues, preserve event identities, branches, and stopping conditions; scenarios do not become actual evidence or authority to act.

Teaching construction: five bounded output layers for the original scenarioTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEverything responds only to the original fictional premise, adding no actual observation or dialogue. Access to existing files is also not assumed.

①Behavior within the premise: one veto occurs in a public meeting; exact words, complete minutes, and specific consequences are unavailable. ②State hypotheses: pressure, fatigue, trust, role responsibility, and longer-term tolerance of uncertainty are candidates without independent support. ③Circles and channels: indicators, resources, and costs of public failure require checking; veto→team response→return→subsequent change in the leader remains only a candidate chain. ④Next material: first examine indicator versions, resource constraints, decision duties, and premeeting information already permitted for this project; assess whether they distinguish candidates, separately checking permission and risk for any necessary new inquiry. ⑤Retained unknowns: inner experience, family circumstances, long-term tendencies, the meaning of silence, and each path's probability remain unsettled. Conditional branches may be proposed, not diagnosis or discipline of actual people.

BoundaryA teaching output format, not findings from an actual investigation. Filling five layers does not certify the theory method's actual benefits.

Mathematical teaching construction: one veto fits two rulesTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThreshold 5, indicator r, and models are mathematical teaching assumptions, not the leader's actual psychology or a real resource standard. Comparability is an explicit premise, not achieved actual evidence.

Let artificial resource indicator r and binary veto Y be given. Candidate A specifies Y=1 if and only if r<5; candidate B specifies constant Y=1. At the sole stipulated scenario r=3, both give Y=1. A future comparable scenario r=7 with identical target, visible information, and other relevant conditions would create a distinguishing opportunity: A gives Y=0, B gives Y=1. Even observing one answer would test only compatibility of these two listed models, without excluding unlisted causes.

BoundaryProves neither A nor B true, authorizes no addition or deprivation of resources for experimentation, and does not turn veto counts into a personality test.

Teaching construction: retain two testable paths after the same eventTeaching scenario

AssumptionsBoth are conditional scenarios, without invented observations, probabilities, or implementation effects.

Path A: if a veto reduces expression safety and members consequently speak less; if that change returns through a specified channel, is interpreted by the leader as successful coercion, and affects later action, a reinforcing path may form. Path B: if an understandable account of resource constraints and an actually responsive review entry point are later provided; if the team revises the plan accordingly and the leader responds, collaborative revision may form. Every “if” requires material. A notice or explanation alone guarantees neither safety, effective review, nor restored trust.

BoundaryThey are neither exhaustive nor ranked. Shared external events, failed return, or other mechanisms may still change what follows.

Experiment 2, 1977: observers must also examine the sample they sawDocumented case

Ross, Amabile, and Steinmetz had two female research assistants reenact 12 selected female quiz pairings from Experiment 1 for 48 student observers. The assistants repeated the reenactments with roles exchanged. After watching, observers rated general knowledge and on average rated questioners above contestants.

SourceRoss et al., Social Roles, Social Control, and Biases in Social-Perception ProcessesJPSP 35(7):485–494, July 1977; Experiment 2: Observers’ Perceptions, printed pp.490–491/PDF 6–7; Personnel and Procedures, and Results.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsThis section adds Experiment 2's observers and the staged material's status, rather than repeating Experiment 1's role-allocation example. It is an experimental reenactment, not an unarranged natural meeting. Observer ratings are not measurements of the assistants' actual overall knowledge, nor evidence of this lesson's leader's motives or a denial of all individual differences.

    If research needs to know caregiving responsibilities, may it demand public disclosure of family circumstances?

  7. 7

    Can the five-layer output directly create disciplinary authority?

If the original says the leader suddenly vetoed something, may angry words be added?

No. The original supplies no specific words, and sudden behavior does not establish inner anger.

Basis: Chinese source line 2071 and the teaching premise's status.

If time pressure is a fast-variable candidate, has it already been established as the cause of the veto?

No. Actual deadlines, perception, and causal-chain material are needed, with other candidates retained.

Basis: Chinese source lines 2071–2073.

If both models veto at r=3, can repeatedly copying that scenario distinguish them?

Not automatically. Comparable conditions yielding different predictions or other distinguishing material are needed.

Basis: Mathematical construction: answers differ only at r=7.

If the team falls silent after a veto, may coercive feedback directly be registered as established?

No. Check causes of silence, return, the leader's uptake, subsequent change, and shared external causes.

Basis: Chinese source line 2073 and §6.2, §9.5.

Are uninvolved observers necessarily unbiased?

Not necessarily. They may still see only a role-selected sample; Ross Experiment 2 provides one bounded experimental observation.

Basis: P-ROSS2 and observational boundaries.

If research needs to know caregiving responsibilities, may it demand public disclosure of family circumstances?

Need does not directly confer authority. First check task relevance, minimum necessary material, permission, and risk, allowing unknowns to remain.

Basis: Chinese source line 2073 and §9.8.

Can the five-layer output directly create disciplinary authority?

No. It may enter conditional-path analysis; diagnosis, punishment, and coercion need independent grounds and authority.

Basis: Chinese source line 2075.

Experiment 2, 1977: observers must also examine the sample they saw

9.11Where This Part Stops ​

The actor state layer can describe which observable states and candidate variables are currently available. It can identify changes that roles and circles may activate and the channels through which individuals and circles constitute one another. It can also describe which time bands a new event may reach first and which information remains unknown or protected by privacy.

This framework does not adjudicate the essence of a person. No professional assessment amounts to an ontological definition of a person. The clinical significance and scope of application of personality descriptions should be assessed by qualified professionals on the basis of relevant evidence, valid authorization, and participation by the people concerned. This framework cannot supply that assessment on its own. Future paths enter conditional foresight. Value and action enter the layer of normative choice and authorization. Prediction, professional status, and labels do not automatically confer authority to act.

9.11Note

Understanding this section

9.11 Where this part stops

A stopping point does not make people incomprehensible black boxes. It specifies the bounded answers this layer can deliver, questions requiring more evidence, and uses requiring separately grounded professional, normative, and authorization procedures.

Chinese source line 2079 first lists five positive capabilities; only line 2081 then states, in translation, “This framework does not adjudicate a person's essence.” Remembering only that prohibition misses this part's actual work: understanding an actor's states and conditions in task-relevant, observable, revisable ways, rather than ending all description. [T-911]

First are current observable states and candidate variables. Recording several recent nonresponses initially establishes only that no reply arrived through a specified channel within a specified window. Fatigue, busyness, channel failure, and unwillingness to communicate remain different candidates. Description specifies material and measurement scope; candidates retain their support levels. A state vector is not a window into the mind, and unknowns cannot automatically become zero or pathology. [T-911；T-state；T-93]

Second are changes potentially activated by roles and circles. Behavior in meetings, family, or public platforms may reflect different responsibilities, resources, visibility, and costs. “Potentially” preserves competing explanations: check role requirements and actual channels rather than infer psychology from a role name or treat all cross-context change as inauthenticity or split personality. [T-911；T-roles]

Third are channels of mutual constitution between individuals and circles. Explain both how rules reach the person and how individual actions alter the group through relations, coordination, resources, or rule processes. Each direction bears its own evidential responsibility. One state description can contain both lines of inquiry, but “mutual influence” alone does not establish a closed loop. [T-911；T-mutual]

Fourth are time bands a new event may reach first. Sudden news may initially change attention and immediate judgment; repeated role demands may alter habits or self-narratives over longer windows. These are conditional path hypotheses. Event intensity or repetition cannot jump directly to long-term personality change. Time of reach, changes in the object, and when we learn of change must still be recorded separately. [T-911；T-times；T-history]

Fifth is explicit unknown status and privacy protection. Unknowns may reflect absent material, nonidentifiability, the person's lack of expression, or material unavailable for this task. Listing these boundaries prevents a seemingly complete profile from hiding key gaps. Privacy is not measurement error; refusal to disclose is not evidence of a problem. Predictive value does not automatically release restricted material. [T-911；T-privacy]

Chinese source line 2081 assigns clinical meaning and applicability of personality descriptions to appropriate professional assessment, naming qualified personnel, corresponding evidence, valid authorization, and participation by the person concerned together. These are not substitutes: credentials do not fill missing evidence; measurement does not expand permission; a signed form does not automatically achieve understandable communication or actual participation. This explains the book's responsibility boundary, not current clinical or legal qualification rules in any jurisdiction. [T-911；T-professional]

Participation does not require the person to handle all expression or every burden of proof alone. Where support is needed, check whether supporters help understanding, submit material, act under delegation, or make substitute decisions. Representative expression is not automatically personal consent. Procedures should address usable communication, refusal, dissent, and continuity of support. Incomplete expression permits neither arbitrary characterization nor interruption of necessary support for registration's sake. [T-support]

Even a fully established professional assessment answers questions within a bounded task, not a final definition of a person's whole existence, value, or future. The teaching projection example illustrates a simple logical obstacle: retaining a few fields may answer one question without recovering every distinction. This mathematical fact proves neither that a particular psychological measurement is invalid nor a philosophical theorem that “human essence does not exist.” [T-911；T-93]

WHO's 2001 ICF distinguishes its classification object from the whole person and sets ethical boundaries for users. This historical normative-text example shows that mature professional classifications also limit interpretive scope. It is neither a validity trial of a personality-diagnosis tool nor experimental support for this framework. Specific claims and locations appear in the case card. [P-ICF]

The latter sentence gives three next directions. “What happens next?” enters conditional foresight, retaining starting points, mechanisms, branches, windows, and unknowns. “What is more worthwhile?” enters normative comparison, stating values, conflicts of interest, and protection floors. “Who may do what?” checks authorization object, scope, conditions, duration, and review action by action. Knowing what may happen does not make an option better; judging it better does not give oneself authority to execute it. [T-911；T-forecast；T-NJ]

Stopping must not become an excuse to delay support. If material already establishes harm requiring protection but complete professional classification is unavailable, record the current problem within its scope, retain uncertainty, and seek low-risk support. This does not permit escalated punishment or public labeling. Any emergency duties come from independently applicable grounds, not temporary creation by an analyst's prediction or label. [T-noinfra；T-professional]

A proper ending therefore gives “bounded delivery with explicit handoff”: deliver five kinds of state-layer answers and their unknowns, identifying the next question type and missing grounds. Chinese source line 2083 merely points to Part X. Subsequent multi-circle joint states expand conditional representation without canceling this section's boundaries concerning professional judgment, privacy, values, and authority. [T-911]

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Use the five capabilities at Chinese source line 2079 as a checklist: current state, role activation, mutual-constitution channels, event time bands, and unknowns/privacy, distinguishing records from candidates item by item.

  2. 2

    Limit every conclusion to actual material, task, window, and permitted use. Moving from description to mechanism adds corresponding distinguishing and causal evidence.

  3. 3

    If clinical interpretation of personality descriptions is required, register professional qualifications, evidence, valid authorization, and participation by the person concerned. None replaces the others.

  4. 4

    Even an established professional assessment does not equate a bounded domain conclusion with a person's entire identity, value, or life trajectory.

  5. 5

    Separate future, values, and execution authority into distinct questions, proceeding to conditional foresight, normative choice, and authorization judgments respectively.

  6. 6

    Retain low-risk routes for actual support. Missing professional conclusions neither erase recordable harm nor permit labeling, punishment, or overreach.

Distinctions to keep clear

State-layer delivery

Five kinds of bounded observation, candidates, and relational explanations.

≠

An ontological definition of a person

These explanations are not assembled into the person's complete essence.

Professional qualifications

One condition required for the corresponding professional work.

≠

Authorization for a specific action

Still requires itemized checking of action, object, scope, duration, and grounds.

Assessment evidence

Material supporting a specific question and applicability scope.

≠

Participation by the person concerned

Understanding, expression, dissent, and support cannot be replaced solely by material quality.

Credible prediction

A future judgment has corresponding grounds under given conditions.

≠

Justified and authorized disposition

Values and authority need additional premises.

Suspending ungrounded judgments

Do not fill gaps with diagnosis or labels for the whole person.

≠

Refusing all support

Do not thereby ignore existing harm and needs for low-risk support.

Mathematical teaching construction: a task representation does not preserve every differenceTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe three fields and two records are entirely constructed, not actual personality indicators; q depending only on a and b is an explicit mathematical premise.

Limit artificial records to three binary fields z=(a,b,c). This is only a record space, not a claim to represent an entire person. The task asks only q(z)=a+b, using representation g(z)=(a,b). For record A=(1,0,0) and record B=(1,0,1), both have g=(1,0) and q=1, but c differs. The representation therefore genuinely suffices for q but cannot answer c; identical g does not imply identical records. If the task later adds a question about c, the representation needs more information or an explicit unknown.

BoundaryProves only the logical limitation of this noninjective projection. It neither invalidates all professional assessments nor treats a mathematical record space as an ontological model of people.

Logical teaching construction: correct prediction without authority to executeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsP and J concern different responsibilities. The assumptions explicitly contain no institutional rule granting permission from predictive correctness. This is a logical countermodel, not an actual case.

Let P mean that a prediction is correct under agreed conditions, and J mean that someone has valid authorization for a particular actual action. The assumptions allow P=true and J=false—for example, an analyst may read public material but has no permission to change another person's arrangements. This assignment alone refutes the claim that P necessarily implies J. Even if J is separately true, it applies only to its declared action scope; one permission cannot extend to disclosing private material or compulsory action.

BoundaryNo actual permissions, emergency duties, or legal exceptions are adjudicated; their applicable grounds require separate checking. Nor does J=true establish effects or normative justification.

Teaching construction: a bounded closing statementTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAn expression exercise containing no actual people or data. “Existing records” is a conditional assumption, not a claim that we actually possess someone's information.

“Existing records support the occurrence of a behavior within the given window; pressure and role conditions remain candidates, and material sufficient to distinguish mechanisms has not been obtained. One possible channel is identified, but subsequent change remains to be checked. Long-term tendencies, inner experience, and protected information remain unknown. Prediction requires explicit conditional branches; clinical explanation belongs in an appropriate procedure with qualifications, evidence, authorization, and the person's participation; changing actual arrangements additionally requires separate treatment of values and execution permissions.”

BoundaryA template cannot replace actual material review. Completing it creates neither professional qualifications nor certification of this framework's effectiveness.

WHO's 2001 ICF: classification boundaries in a professional textDocumented case

WHO published the ICF in 2001. Introduction §3.3 explains that it classifies health and health-related states and places descriptions within environmental and personal contexts. Annex 6 item 2 opposes identifying an entire person solely through categories; items 5–6 call, where possible, for explaining purposes and allowing participation and challenges to assessment; item 11 reminds readers that individuals in the same category may still differ in many ways.

SourceWHO，International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health（2001）ISBN 92 4 154542 9; Introduction §3.3, printed p. 8/PDF 12; Annex 6 items 2, 5, 6, 11, printed pp. 244–245/PDF 248–249.Reading scope: Partly read

Scope and limitsA public copy of the original 2001 classification and ethics text, proving only that the text explicitly states these boundaries. It is not a clinical personality trial, does not assess current cases or current law, and does not establish actual compliance. Hosting the copy in a 2024 directory does not alter its 2001 publication identity. The WHO direct link failed during access; no claim is made to have read the entire book through the official entry point.

International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health: ICF

What does not follow

  • Boundary in the original: candidate states are not established psychological mechanisms; one behavior cannot directly establish a long-term personality hypothesis.
  • Mathematical teaching counterexample: two complete artificial records share a selected projection yet differ in omitted fields. Equal projections do not imply equality of every feature.
  • Logical teaching counterexample: a true prediction and an implementer lacking authority for the corresponding action can coexist. Prediction truth therefore does not imply authority to execute.
  • Boundary in the original: qualified professional status confers no authority over the person's entire life. Bounded professional conclusions are not ontological definitions of a person.
  • Boundary in the original: incomplete clinical classification does not mean current harm is unrecordable. Low-risk support does not permit punishment, dossier creation, public labeling, or resource deprivation.
  • Actual-literature boundary: the existence of ethical requirements in the 2001 ICF does not prove compliance in every actual use or provide diagnostic, proxy, or permission conclusions for current cases.

Scope and open questions

This unit concerns methodological judgment. Actual sources support only the listed facts; the diagram and teaching construction each retain their own status.

  • This lesson proposes no diagnosis or action plan for an actual person. Applying it to a case still requires separate confirmation of qualifications, evidence, valid authorization, and participation arrangements for the specific professional task and applicable procedures.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Does completing a current-state table provide a complete personality definition of the person?

  2. 2

    Does a professional license suffice to authorize public disclosure of a person's assessment records?

  3. 3

    If two artificial records have identical g, why must q match while c need not?

  4. 4

    May very accurate prediction lead directly to compulsory execution?

  5. 5

    If a complete clinical assessment is unavailable, should recording ongoing harm stop?

  6. 6

    If a proxy completes an assessment form, may it always be treated as the person's consent?

  7. 7

    Does the ICF ethical appendix prove that actual classifications have never harmed people?

Does completing a current-state table provide a complete personality definition of the person?

No. Completed fields do not prove measurement validity, and a bounded task representation is not a person's entire essence.

Basis: Chinese source lines 2079–2081 and the projection construction.

Does a professional license suffice to authorize public disclosure of a person's assessment records?

No. Professional qualifications do not replace valid grounds and scope for a specific disclosure action.

Basis: Chinese source line 2081 and §14.6, §16.13.

If two artificial records have identical g, why must q match while c need not?

q depends only on retained a and b, while g does not retain c; c equals 0 and 1 respectively in the example.

Basis: The teaching example q=a+b and projection g=(a,b).

May very accurate prediction lead directly to compulsory execution?

No. Future judgments, normative comparisons, and action authorization are different questions; predictive accuracy does not supply the latter two.

Basis: Chinese source line 2081 and the logical countermodel.

If a complete clinical assessment is unavailable, should recording ongoing harm stop?

That does not follow. Current problems may be recorded within the material's scope and low-risk support sought, without upgrading to diagnosis, punishment, or public characterization.

Basis: §16.11、§16.13。

If a proxy completes an assessment form, may it always be treated as the person's consent?

No. Distinguish the proxy matter, grounds, and scope, preserving the person's communication, objections, and support conditions.

Basis: §16.12。

Does the ICF ethical appendix prove that actual classifications have never harmed people?

No. A normative text states how something should be used; its provisions alone prove neither actual compliance nor effects of use.

Basis: The normative-text status and boundaries of P-ICF.
